jobs.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. PRODUCTION game sprite atlas with TRUE ALPHA transparent background, not a concept board. One horizontal row of independent sprites, all fully visible with at least 8 percent empty margins top/bottom and clear transparent gaps between items. No framing, caption, panels, landscape, ground, shadows or extra props. First input is the user's APPROVED PIXEL STYLE; use ONLY its item rendering style, not the board or lettering. Subsequent inputs are SHAPE/IDENTITY references. Redraw from scratch in this fine but unmistakable 16-bit pixel art style. Tall items logical 90–110 pixels high, enlarged as crisp square clusters. At normal game size they must read as hand-placed pixel art, not detailed painted sprites. Limited 6–8 tones per material, stepwise flat highlight bands, visible pixel stair steps, restrained gold/champagne highlights with cool steel shadows. NO smooth gradients, NO anti-aliased outlines, NO photo textures, NO speckled or dithering noise. Preserve the exact referenced shape, proportions, label design and identifying motifs, simplified into deliberate pixel clusters. Refine beyond generic chunky 32px icons. Do not crop ANY cap, rim, foot or handle. Exactly FOUR objects, left-to-right: OPEN tapered silver shaker BODY WITHOUT LID; gold double-ended hourglass jigger with small 30 and15 marks; SEPARATE domed silver strainer lid with narrow cylindrical perforated neck; SEPARATE small round silver cap. The four parts must be independently extractable, no assembled shaker. Preserve shape/aspect ratio of each object in input2. Shaker body has about 6 bold vertically broken reflection bands and a narrow bottom seam, transparent background, solid steel body; lid holes truly transparent. Jigger rims thin and stepped, solid gold body, dark empty interior.
